# Choosing a license for CFS

The repository `briefcasejona/CFS` is **public** and has **no LICENSE** file. Without one, the code is "all rights reserved": people can view it (and fork it on GitHub under GitHub's terms) but may not legally reuse, modify or redistribute it.

| Option | Lets others… | Good when | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Proprietary** (`LICENSE`: "Copyright … All rights reserved") | View only | You may sell the app or want full control | Clearest to state it explicitly |
| **MIT** | Do almost anything, keep the notice | You want contributions and don't mind commercial reuse/forks | Most common, simplest |
| **Apache-2.0** | Same as MIT + explicit patent grant | Same as MIT, slightly more formal | |
| **GPL-3.0 / AGPL-3.0** | Reuse only if they share their changes too | You want forks to stay open | |
| **Source-available (e.g. PolyForm Noncommercial)** | View/use non-commercially | Openness without commercial copies | Not "open source" by OSI definition |

Dependency check: code dependencies are all MIT — no constraint. **Assets are a separate matter:** `assets/models/cc-by-nc-sa/` is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (third-party) whatever the code license is; the LICENSE should say that this folder is excluded and keeps its own license. Natural Earth / terrain data keep their own terms (`assets/theaters/europe/SOURCES.md`).

Also note: as long as the CC BY-NC-SA models are shipped, the game as distributed must stay **non-commercial** (no paid version, no ads). To monetize later, remove/replace those models first (and talk to a lawyer — see the company profile's escalation rules).

**Recommendation:** MIT for the code (simplest; friends can fork and mod it) with a clear "assets/models/cc-by-nc-sa is licensed separately under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0" clause — or "All rights reserved" if you might sell CFS one day. — **Decision (Jonathan):** pending
